title: Familiar Game Controls: Designing Remapping and Device Changes

scenes.title: 전체 내용 안내
lines: When making a new game, which familiar controls should you keep, and what should you design anew?
We will examine movement and kicking in Anger Foot, the actions in Gunbrella, then movement and aiming in My Friend Pedro.
By the end, you can review your controls by separating familiar conventions, button assignments and the functions of an input device.
Let us start with turning the view toward a target and kicking.

scenes.title: 익숙한 관점에서 새 행동을 본다
lines: In Anger Foot, the view turns toward a target while the character approaches, fires or kicks.
Watch the aim shift between targets in the room and above. Kicking joins movement and aiming.
These pixels do not reveal the exact keys or their order. What we can examine is the relationship between actions.
When designing around familiar first-person controls, begin with how a new action connects to the existing ones.

scenes.title: 익숙한 약속을 설계의 출발점으로
lines: A control convention is an expectation about the kind of action an input will produce.
For someone who knows that convention, keeping inputs consistent with their roles provides a starting point.
Novelty can come from enemy positions, routes and situations that combine actions. Every button need not become unfamiliar.
Do not assume a newcomer already knows the convention. Check the new action and the guidance it needs separately.

scenes.title: 발차기를 더해도 방향 관계는 남는다
lines: Across the corridor and room shots, follow how targets stay in view as the character approaches and kicks.
Establishing a direction and acting on a nearby target connect, but they serve different functions.
In your design, check both where to assign a kick and whether it can be performed alongside movement or aiming.
These are separate trailer shots. We do not treat them as one continuous input sequence or a prescribed strategy.

scenes.title: 버튼 재배치는 행동의 연결을 옮긴다
lines: Remapping changes the assignment between an input and an action. It does not remove the action itself.
In a hypothetical design, after moving jump to another button, test the combination of moving and jumping.
If one button has different roles in different contexts, update those assignments and the on-screen prompts together.
Do not stop at a changed menu assignment. Check actions needed together and the prompts after remapping.

scenes.title: 우산 동작을 이동과 나누어 관찰한다
lines: In Gunbrella, the character moves and jumps, opens the umbrella and changes the direction of attack.
Watch the umbrella open in the air, then the aim turn upward. One tool can serve several actions.
We are separating visible actions here, not verifying the current game’s key assignments or remapping features.
For your own design, list movement, jumping, tool use and aiming, then connect the actions needed together.
Opening the umbrella does not by itself establish that every attack is blocked. Check input relationships and action outcomes separately.

scenes.title: 장치가 바뀌면 기능도 대조한다
lines: Distinguish moving a button assignment from changing the functions an input device provides.
A simple button gives pressed and released states, while aiming may need a continuously changing direction or position.
Assigning the name “aim” to a button does not automatically transfer the function that determines direction.
Before naming the input, write what must be selected, over what range, and how continuously it must change.

scenes.title: 몸의 이동과 총의 방향이 갈라진다
lines: In My Friend Pedro, the body descends or moves sideways while a gun points elsewhere.
Across the barrel and hanging shots, follow movement and target direction separately.
Some shots show two guns pointing in different directions. The question involves both executing an action and choosing its target.
This observation does not prove the exact input method or supported devices. It illustrates the design problem of selecting a direction.
When moving to a new device, decide separately how to provide target changes while moving.

scenes.title: 대체 입력은 선택의 범위를 바꿀 수 있다
lines: Hypothetical alternatives include choosing a direction directly, cycling through candidate targets and assisting automatic selection.
These methods do not always produce the same result. They change which targets can be selected and how selection happens.
Whichever method you choose, test whether the intended selection is possible when movement and target changes are needed together.
Go beyond preserving an action’s name. Check whether you preserved the decisions the player needs to make.

scenes.title: 연속 동작 속에서 기능을 점검한다
lines: Unlike the earlier short shots, this multi-floor combat interval lets us follow the same traversal continuously.
Watch the guns point left and right, then above and below across the floor grates.
The target direction changes while the body moves. Keeping movement buttons alone does not preserve every required control function.
In your own design, execute these combinations one by one and check target selection and prompt consistency.
Test whether the convention holds on a new route and with different targets, rather than replaying one scene to make it look familiar.

scenes.title: 익숙한 약속과 새 결정을 함께 설계하기
lines: To use familiar controls, preserve the roles of inputs and connect newly added actions clearly.
When remapping, check combined actions and prompts. When changing devices, check direction and target-selection functions.
Finally, try a different route and check whether the intended decisions remain possible. That helps distinguish what to keep from what to redesign.
